newsitem.title: USA: Miami deficit may be $60 mln, emergency order.
newsitem.headline: Miami deficit may be $60 mln, emergency order.

text.p: City Manager Merrett Stierheim asked Miami city commissioners to declare a fiscal emergency, and said the city's budget shortfall could be as high as $60 million.
The emergency declaration will be considered at a special budget meeting on Monday and would allow the city to open negotiations with its employee unions.

Stierheim initially estimated the shortfall in the city's $275 million operating budget for fiscal 1997 at $38.9 million. But in a memo Tuesday, he said the earlier report did not include captial improvement liabilities, some of which are contractual and "will add many more millions to the city's shortfall."
At a Tuesday night meeting, Steirheim told commissioners the deficit could be as high as $60 million.
Stierheim also recommended that the city commission ask the city attorney to pursue legal action against former Finance Director Manohar Surana, who resigned in August.
Stierheim was unavailable for comment Wednesday and the memo did not elaborate on possible grounds for action against Surana, who controlled both budget and finance operations.
Shortly after Surana's resignation, federal prosecutors said he was cooperating in an investigation of alleged kickbacks involving city contracts, and would plead guilty to unspecified charges.

City Manager Cesar Odio, Commissioner Miller Dawkins and a lobbyist were charged with bribery and conspiracy in connection with the allegations. Prosecutors said Surana had worn a hidden wire to record conversations that allegedly implicted the three.
In his memo Tuesday, Stierheim also recommended that the city issue $25 million of tax anticipation notes instead of the $15 million originally planned.

He recommended that the city raise garbage collection, license and franchise fees; close some little-used public facilities, increase parking ticket enforcement, and cut support for some community organizations.
The commission was scheduled to consider those recommendations at Monday's meeting.

In a separate memo to assistant city managers and department heads Tuesday, Stierheim ordered 200 employees to return city-owned or leased vehicles, rescinded all city gasoline cards, cancelled cellular phone allowances, tightened overtime rules, restricted purchasing and froze hiring and salaries.
He asked department heads to remove certain non-productive city workers by the close of business Friday, specifically those who got their jobs "for reasons other than merit."

The memo notes that in personal discussions and at budget hearings last week, several directors had "talked or hinted" that such employees had been placed in thier departments. There was no indication how many employees were involved.
